egress.terms: Free and mirrored: `download.savannah.{gnu,nongnu}.org` redirect to a world-wide mirror ring. Verified live: a GET 302s to a national mirror (fosszone.csd.auth.gr) which serves 200 with real bytes. No metering, no billing.

record.tooling: SSH public-key auth only. Upload via scp (the -O flag is mandatory, see limits) or rsync to download.savannah.nongnu.org releases directory. Removal via restricted SSH commands ssh host rm or rmdir. Gnulib build-aux gnupload script is supported. Read side is plain anonymous HTTP from the mirror ring.
record.chaining: One Savannah group per project, unlimited files per group, unlimited versions retained forever. Accounts are free; the gate is that a human evaluates the package ('Evaluate and approve non-gnu packages submitted for hosting'), so cardinality is bounded by reviewer throughput, not by quota. For GNU packages ftp.gnu.org/alpha.gnu.org is a second surface with an automated signed-upload path.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap: none published. Structural caps that matter more: (1) SFTP IS DISABLED - announced 2023-11, 'we've found a vulnerability in our SFTP setup, and couldn't fix it otherwise than completely disabling SFTP. This affects uploading files to the download host'. Because OpenSSH >= 9.0 makes scp use SFTP by default, `scp -O` is required or every upload fails. (2) GPG-signing is expected (the docs tell you to upload foo.tar.gz + foo.tar.gz.sig) though not enforced: 'unlike ftp.gnu.org, Savannah doesn't enforce using GPG signatures for releases'. (3) Write access requires a registered SSH key on the account.
record.reliability_note: Two real breakages. First, SFTP-off is a live trap for any modern client - a naive `scp` on OpenSSH 9+ silently fails. Second, the mirror ring is uneven: the same lzip tarball (123,850 bytes) took 4.6 s once and timed out at 21 s on the redirect target (ftp.cc.uoc.gr) another time, so per-mirror health varies and single-stream fetch is not trustworthy. Site pages also intermittently serve a Kant-quoting anti-scraper page instead of content - the register/ and requirements.php URLs both did this via the reader while the Wayback copy of the same page was clean.

record.notes: No published byte quota found on any Savannah page - the hosting-requirements doc speaks only in terms of purpose ('The space given to you on this server is given for the expressed purpose of advancing free software') and permanence ('Our intent is to provide a permanent home for all versions of your project'), never a number. Disk was moved to Ceph/NFS precisely to remove the old ceiling (savannah-hackers-public, 2019-04: 'This increases the disk space and moves onto the new cephs storage').
